title: Requirements Engineering
course_context: Undergraduate demonstration lesson; all content is supplied through configuration.

objectives.title: Classify and evaluate requirements
objectives.description: Distinguish functional behavior from non-functional quality constraints and explain measurable, consistent requirements.
success_criteria: Recognizes testable conditions and conflicting limits
objectives.diagnostic_prompt: Classify a fresh behavior and quality constraint and justify each classification.

misconceptions.description: A quality constraint limits how behavior occurs; it is not a new function.
misconceptions.counterexample: Sending a receipt specifies an action; a two-second delivery limit constrains the action.

required_task.title: Reflection
required_task.description: Reflect on what you can explain or do now.
required_task.submission_prompt: What can you explain or do now that you could not before?

study_resources.title: How to Write a Good Requirement
study_resources.description: A checklist for clear and verifiable requirements.
study_resources.focus: Look for measurable wording, consistency, and conditions that allow a repeatable test.

diagnostic_quiz.question: Which requirement specifies a functional behavior?
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: Sending a receipt specifies an observable action.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: Identify what the system does, rather than how well it does it.
distractor_misconceptions: Misapplies functional behavior: Respond within two seconds
Misapplies functional behavior: Limit memory use to 100 MB

diagnostic_quiz.question: Why is a response-time limit non-functional?
options: It adds a new user action
It constrains how quickly an existing behavior occurs
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: Response time is a quality constraint on existing behavior.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: Separate a system action from a quality limit on that action.
distractor_misconceptions: Misapplies quality constraints: It adds a new user action
Misapplies quality constraints: It cannot be tested
Misapplies quality constraints: It describes the programming language

diagnostic_quiz.question: Which version of “search should be fast” is directly testable?
options: 95% of searches finish within two seconds under 100 simultaneous users
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: A threshold and defined load allow a repeatable performance test.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: A test needs an observable outcome and specified conditions.
distractor_misconceptions: Misapplies measurable conditions: Search is extremely fast
Misapplies measurable conditions: Use a new database
Misapplies measurable conditions: Search should be pleasant

diagnostic_quiz.question: One statement permits five seconds and another requires one second for the same search under the same conditions. What should the team do?
options: Reconcile the conflicting limits with stakeholders
Choose whichever is easier without discussion
Ignore both because performance is non-functional
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: Reconcile conflicting limits and agree on one condition that can be verified.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: Ask whether the conditions allow both statements to be true at the same time.
distractor_misconceptions: Misapplies conflicting requirements: Choose whichever is easier without discussion
Misapplies conflicting requirements: Implement both with no clarification
Misapplies conflicting requirements: Ignore both because performance is non-functional

reasoning_rubric.description: Explains how to resolve a conflict

diagnostic_quiz.question: A project proposes 100% uptime at no extra cost. Which is the strongest next step?
options: Treat ambition as evidence of feasibility
Analyze failure scenarios, feasibility, cost, and reliability trade-offs with stakeholders
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: Reliability targets require feasibility analysis and explicit trade-offs.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: A useful target must consider the consequences of failure and the resources needed.
distractor_misconceptions: Misapplies feasibility and trade-offs: Promise it without checking
Misapplies feasibility and trade-offs: Remove every quality requirement
Misapplies feasibility and trade-offs: Treat ambition as evidence of feasibility

reasoning_rubric.description: Uses feasibility and trade-offs to justify a target

learning_assets.explanation: Ask what action the system performs, then ask what limit applies to that action. The action is functional; a quality limit is non-functional.
learning_assets.worked_example: A shop emails a receipt after payment (functional behavior) and sends it within two seconds (non-functional performance constraint).
learning_assets.analogy: A restaurant order names the dish; a ten-minute service limit constrains its delivery. This comparison simplifies how software requirements are specified.
learning_assets.counterexample: A fast response without emailing the receipt meets a timing goal but misses the required action. Correct behavior with a late receipt can miss the timing constraint.

foundational.prompt: A library performs loan renewal and confirms it within 3 seconds. Classify the behavior and the limit, and justify each.
foundational.hint: Separate the action from the condition on its delivery.

foundational.prompt: A library must perform loan renewal and respond within 3 seconds under a load of 100 requests. Explain which requirement constrains quality and why.
foundational.hint: Identify what happens and how its quality is constrained.

foundational.prompt: Rewrite “the library should respond quickly” using an observable response, a numerical threshold, and a load of 100 concurrent requests. Explain how to test it.
foundational.hint: A test needs an observable outcome, a threshold, and conditions.

rubric.description: Defines an observable response and numerical threshold

foundational.prompt: One specification permits 3 seconds for loan renewal; another permits 6 seconds under identical conditions. Explain the conflict and how you would resolve it with stakeholders.
foundational.hint: Check the shared conditions, then consider how the limits can be agreed.

rubric.description: Explains how to resolve a conflict

foundational.prompt: The library proposes zero downtime while cutting its operating budget. Explain what feasibility evidence is needed and how cost and reliability affect the decision.
foundational.hint: Compare the proposed target with failure scenarios and available resources.

rubric.description: Uses feasibility and trade-offs to justify a target

topic_introduction: Requirements describe what a system must do and the conditions it must satisfy. Clear, measurable requirements make behavior and quality expectations testable.
approved_material: Functional requirements specify observable behavior. Non-functional requirements constrain quality, such as response time, reliability, and resource use. Measurable conditions define an outcome, threshold and load. Conflicting limits under the same conditions must be reconciled with stakeholders. Reliability targets need feasibility analysis and explicit trade-offs between cost and risk.
introductory_example: Emailing a payment receipt is a behavior; delivering it within two seconds is a quality constraint.
prerequisite_knowledge: Basic reading and arithmetic; no prior subject knowledge is required.
